reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 shows low wear in a different alloy via a nanohierarchical architecture, not a reactive additive. E2 is incomplete and discusses low friction in UHV for an unmodified HEA, not a self-lubricating tribofilm. E3 shows improved wear resistance in a coating via W-rich intermetallics, not an in situ lubricious phase. None of the evidence supports the specific mechanism of additive-induced tribofilm formation, grain boundary sliding, or continuous regeneration in CoCrFeNi.
premises: A reactive additive can in situ form a high-temperature stable, self-lubricating tribofilm in CoCrFeNi during sliding.
This tribofilm lowers interfacial shear strength and reduces friction and wear.
Shear-induced grain refinement activates grain boundary sliding (inverse Hall-Petch) to further reduce friction and wear.
The tribofilm continuously regenerates and adapts to temperature and load variations.
The modified alloy will show consistently lower friction and wear than unmodified CoCrFeNi from RT to 800 °C.
